neighbours.label: being 'on' someone's list: ' list' / ' of' in 'on my must-see list', 'on the list of ...' (membership in a list or set, not the noun list in general)
fire: If you love old castles, Edinburgh belongs on your must-visit list this summer.
Two more pesticides were placed on the list of chemicals restricted in Europe.
A hike to the crater lake has been on my bucket list for years.
The snow leopard remains on the list of endangered species in Central Asia.
That little bakery in Porto is high on our list of favourite places.
The senator's name was on the list of speakers for the evening session.
Learning to sail is still on her to-do list after all these years.
Three of his novels are on the school's recommended reading list.
quiet: If you love old castles, Edinburgh has a fine one above the old town.
The clerk typed a list with the names of the chemicals made in Europe.
A hike to the crater lake took us most of a long summer day.
He wrote a short list and pinned it to the door of the barn.
That little bakery in Porto sells the best custard tarts we tasted.
The list ran to four pages, and the speaker read every line aloud.
Learning to sail took her two summers and a great deal of patience.
Please list three of his novels and say which one you liked best.

notes: Card: ' list' x8, ' of' x5 (after 'on the list'), ' those' x4. Probes: on your must-see list 0.93, on my list of places 0.91, on the list of banned substances 0.64, required reading lists 0.67, among those who 0.64; but 'made a list of groceries' 0.07 and 'The list was long' 0.01. One leak: 'should be on your itinerary' 0.47 (peak ' your'), so 'be on your ...' already anticipates it. Near misses use the word list outside the on-the-list frame.
